entry.reasons: The entry accurately represents the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation as presented in Topic 8.9 (8.9.A.1) and referenced in Topic 8.4 (8.4.A.2). All symbols in the formula are correctly defined with appropriate units/meanings, and the caution correctly incorporates the exclusion statements regarding derivation and computation of pH changes upon addition of acid/base.

The formula and all four symbol definitions match 8.9.A.1: “pH = pKa + log([A−]/[HA]).” Topic 8.4 first requires its use: 8.4.A.2 says buffer pH “can be determined from the Henderson-Hasselbalch (H−H) equation (see 8.9.A.1),” and 8.4.A.3 also uses it. Topic 8.9 states the equation. The caution correctly reflects both 8.9.A.1 exclusion statements: derivation and computation of the pH change on adding acid or base to a buffer are not assessed.

a_factual: The formula matches the CED EQN under 8.9.A.1 exactly: pH = pKa + log([A−]/[HA]). All four symbols (pH, pKa, [A−], [HA]) are defined, and no extra symbols appear. The meanings match the CED: pKa is the negative log of Ka for the weak acid, and [A−] and [HA] are the conjugate base and weak acid of the pair. Units are correct: pH and pKa are unitless, and the concentrations are in mol/L (the ratio is dimensionless). b_topic_codes: 8.4.A.2 and 8.4.A.3 state that buffer pH 'can be determined from the Henderson-Hasselbalch (H−H) equation (see 8.9.A.1)', so 8.4 is the first place in the unit that requires it and both 8.4 and 8.9 use it. c_ced_required: 8.9.A.1 states 'The pH of the buffer is related to the pKa of the acid and the concentration ratio of the conjugate acid-base pair... described by the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation', and LO 8.9.A requires identifying buffer pH from the conjugate pair. d_caution: The caution matches the CED exclusion statements under 8.9.A.1 (derivation of H-H not assessed; computation of pH change on adding acid or base to a buffer not assessed). No hooks are present.
